copy.h1: SUV rental in Toronto for families, luggage and winter

We confirm the car and the full price in an offer, then deliver it to your door or hand it over at our location once you approve.

sections.heading: Picking a size
sections.body: Compact SUVs carry 4 or 5 people and are easy to park downtown. Most of ours seat 5, and larger models have more space behind the back seats. Some have all-wheel drive, which helps on snowy side streets and cottage roads. Each car's page lists its seats and drive. For more than 5 people, look at our 7 seat cars instead.

sections.heading: Driving in winter

Winter tires make a real difference, and you can ask for them in your request: the fee is {{winter}} a day, capped at {{winterCap}}. Leave extra time, clear the windows and lights before you set off, and check the forecast before a trip to cottage country.

sections.heading: Children and luggage

copy.h1: Car rental under 25 in Toronto
copy.intro: Being under 25 does not close the door on a rental car at CarmaCars. Every car in our fleet takes drivers {{minAge}} and older with an Ontario {{licence}} licence, G or G2. Drivers under {{fullAge}} pay a young driver fee for each day, and each car shows its own fee on its page, so you know the cost before you ask. Your offer lists the full price with the fee included, and you pay only if you approve it.

sections.heading: How the young driver fee works
sections.body: There are two age bands, {{youngA}} and {{youngB}}. The usual fee is {{ydA}} a day for the first and {{ydB}} a day for the second, and some cars have their own amount. It is added for each rental day as a separate line in your offer, with no maximum. An additional driver under {{fullAge}} pays it as well, on top of the additional driver fee.

sections.heading: What you bring

Before pickup you upload photos of your licence and a selfie, and at the handover we check the original licence and the card. If you are 21 with a G2, that is enough for every car.

sections.heading: Keeping the total down
sections.body: A trip of {{weekFrom}} days or more uses the weekly rate, and shorter trips never cost more than it. Collecting the car from our location costs nothing, while delivery adds the car's delivery fee. Bring the car back with the fuel it had, stay within the kilometres included, and skip the 407 ETR unless you are ready to pay its tolls plus {{tollFee}} for each notice.

copy.h1: Weekend car rental in Toronto
copy.intro: A weekend car is how a lot of Torontonians without a car get away: a cottage, a wedding, a visit home or a day at the beach. We can bring the car to you on Friday evening and collect it on Sunday night or Monday morning. Every car on this page shows its weekend day rate, which applies to rental days that start on a Friday or a Saturday. Send a request and your offer shows the full price before you pay.

sections.heading: How weekend days are priced
sections.body: A rental day is 24 hours from your pickup time. A day that starts on a Friday or a Saturday is charged at the car's weekend day rate, and any other day at its daily rate. Your offer lists each day with the rate applied, so the total is clear before you approve. HST is added.

sections.heading: Long weekends book up early
sections.body: Summer long weekends and the holidays go first. A request does not hold the car until you approve the offer, sign and pay, so send it early and approve promptly when the offer arrives. If someone else confirms the same car for the same dates before you, we offer you another car or other dates.

sections.heading: Friday drop-off, Sunday pickup
sections.body: Tell us in your request when and where you want the car. For a condo, add the visitor parking details so the handover is quick. On Sunday or Monday we can collect the car from the same address for its return pickup fee, or you can return it to our location at no charge. Plan the drive home around the kilometres included.

faq.question: Which days count as weekend days?
faq.answer: Any rental day that starts on a Friday or a Saturday is charged at the weekend day rate.

faq.question: Can I pick up on Friday evening?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose your pickup time in the request, and we confirm it in your offer.

faq.question: Is the car held once I send a request?
faq.answer: No. It is booked once you approve the offer, sign and pay.

faq.question: Can I drive to a cottage?
faq.answer: Yes, anywhere in Ontario. Check the kilometres included on the car's page.

copy.h1: Weekly car rental in Toronto
copy.intro: A week is the length many of our renters choose: family in town, a road trip around Ontario, or a stretch of work outside the city. Every car on this page shows its weekly rate on its card and its page. Send a request with your dates, and we confirm the car and the full price in an offer. You pay only once you approve it. We deliver the car to your home, hotel or office, or you collect it from our location at no charge.

sections.heading: The weekly cap
sections.body: Daily rates add up quickly, so we cap them. A trip of 1 to {{weekFromLess1}} days never costs more than the car's weekly rate, and a trip of {{weekFrom}} days or more is priced from the weekly rate. Your offer shows which rate applies to each day before you pay, so there are no surprises on the statement.

sections.heading: Kilometres over a whole week
sections.body: Each car has a daily allowance of kilometres. For a week it is added up: the allowance times the days you book. Drive a long way on the first day and a little on the rest, and you stay inside it. Past the allowance, each extra kilometre is charged at the rate on the car's page.

sections.heading: Where a week can take you
sections.body: The car can go anywhere in Ontario, from Niagara to Muskoka, Ottawa, Prince Edward County or Georgian Bay. Crossing into Quebec or the United States needs our written agreement first, so mention it in your request. Before a long trip, check the kilometres included and plan your stops, since a long return drive uses a good share of a week's allowance.

faq.question: Is a weekly rental cheaper than paying by the day?
faq.answer: Usually. A trip of 1 to {{weekFromLess1}} days is capped at the weekly rate, so a shorter trip never costs more than a week.

faq.question: Can I extend a weekly rental?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for an extension before your return time. We price it, and you pay before the current return time.

faq.question: What if I bring the car back early?
faq.answer: You can, but the rental charge for the booked days is not reduced. The agreement explains early returns.

faq.question: Do you deliver for weekly rentals?
faq.answer: Yes. Delivery to your address costs the car's delivery fee, shown on its page.

copy.h1: Electric and hybrid car rental in Toronto
copy.intro: Renting an electric or hybrid car is a simple way to try driving with less gas, or to keep fuel costs down on a longer rental. The cars on this page are the electric, plug-in hybrid and hybrid cars in our fleet, each with its own page, rates and calendar. When none is listed, none is available right now. Send a request with your dates, and we confirm the car and the full price before you pay.

sections.heading: The charging rule
sections.body: Bring an electric car back with the charge it had at pickup. You do not need to fill it up. If it comes back lower, recharging costs {{evPer}} for each 10% of battery, plus a {{fuelFee}} service fee. At the handover we show you the car's charging port and cable, so you know what to plug into.

sections.heading: Hybrids fill up like any car
sections.body: A regular hybrid runs on gas and charges its own battery as you drive, so there is nothing to plug in. A plug-in hybrid can be charged for some driving on electricity and then runs on gas. Either way, return the car with the fuel it had at pickup, as you would any other rental.

sections.heading: Cold weather planning
sections.body: Cold weather reduces how far an electric car goes on a charge, so plan a longer winter trip with a charging stop. Warming the car while it is still plugged in helps, and so does a slightly cooler cabin on the highway. A hybrid is not affected in the same way, which makes it the easier pick for a long winter drive.

faq.question: Must I return an electric car fully charged?
faq.answer: No. Return it with the charge it had at pickup.

faq.question: What if it comes back with less charge?
faq.answer: Recharging costs {{evPer}} for each 10% of battery, plus a {{fuelFee}} service fee.

faq.question: Do hybrids need to be plugged in?
faq.answer: A regular hybrid never does. A plug-in hybrid can be, but it also runs on gas.

faq.question: Are there electric cars available now?
faq.answer: The cars on this page are the ones available now. When none are listed, browse the whole fleet.
